title: KV orbit calibration & sensitivity scan for INT8/FP8 profiles
creator: Ravi Desai
description: Goal: run a structured calibration and sensitivity scan for kv-cache quantization profiles (FP8 and INT8) to surface per-workload quality regressions and latency/throughput trade-offs. This ticket coordinates the two-stage calibration pipeline (offline sweep + online shadow validation), the sampling strategy for calibration corpora, and the evaluation suite that will decide safe-to-roll profiles. This is an experiment-first ticket: expected outputs are reproducible artifacts (calibration configs, score matrices, dashboards), a recommended default profile per SLO tier, and a short runbook for periodic recalibration.
objective: Find per-model and per-workload KV quantization profiles that minimize memory and latency while bounding quality regression to <1% absolute on critical metrics for production instruction-following and retrieval QA workloads.
experiment_design: Two-stage calibration: 1) offline sweep across global vs per-layer scale, clipping thresholds, and asymmetric rounding; 2) 48-hour shadow validation on sampled production traffic.
Profile space: FP8-e4m3 and INT8 symmetric/asymmetric with per-head outlier clipping and optional per-layer scale factors.
Workloads: instruction-following prompts, long-context summarization (8k tokens), retrieval-augmented QA, and short-chat latency-sensitive traffic.
Batching matrix: batch sizes {1,4,8,16} to measure batching-latency interactions with KV precision.
Metric sweep: for each profile measure token-latency p50/p95/p99, end-to-end throughput, model output similarity (embedding cosine), logit-diff tail statistics, and downstream task accuracy (QA F1).
Holdout sets: 10% of prompts reserved as unseen calibration holdout for final validation; separate adversarial prompt bucket targeting commonsense and arithmetic where quantization often regresses.
Resource isolation: run experiments on a dedicated GPU pool to avoid noisy neighbors affecting latency signals.
calibration_dataset: Stratified samples from production traces (length bins: 0-128, 129-1024, 1025-4096, 4097-8192), with 40% weight on long-context workloads.
Synthetic stress prompts designed to trigger KV outliers (repeated tokens, improbable context switches, high-entropy prefixes).
Public evals for semantic similarity and question answering for cross-checking (SQuAD-like and NQ subsets).
Small labeled set for human-evaluated instruction following (200 examples), used for final binary gating.
Calibration sample size target: ~20k sequences distributed across models and length buckets.
evaluation_metrics: Quality: embedding cosine similarity on generated completions (mean + 5th percentile), QA F1, and instruction-following pass rate (human check).
Logit delta distribution: fraction of tokens where top-1 logit drop > X (tail metric).
Token-level divergence: top-k token overlap and perplexity ratio vs FP32 baseline.
Operational: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec throughput, memory footprint (KV size in GB), and cold-start cache penalty.
Safety gate: if instruction-following pass rate drops >1.0 absolute on human set -> profile rejected.
early_results: Preliminary offline sweep completed for two models (redwood-7b and open-13b). FP8 (e4m3-ish) reduces KV memory by ~2.05x and improves p50 token latency by 12-15% at batch=8. INT8 symmetric yields ~1.9x memory reduction and slightly higher latency improvements (~16-22% p50) but shows outsized quality drops on long-context summarization: embedding cosine mean decreases 0.018 (redwood-7b) and QA F1 drops 2.1 points on the long-context holdout. Observed an interaction between batch size and tail logit-drop: at batch>=8 INT8 exhibits heavier tail regressions on repeated-token stress prompts. FP8 shows smaller tail sensitivity but slightly higher variance across layers, pointing to potential benefit of per-layer scaling. These results are from isolated runs (no shadow traffic) and will be validated in the planned 48h shadow run.
decisions: Adopt two-stage pipeline (offline sweep -> short shadow validation) as gating mechanism before canary rollouts.
Default to FP8 profile for latency-sensitive SLO tier with per-layer fallback to higher precision for identified sensitive layers.
INT8 profiles to be considered only for batch-oriented, throughput-first clusters after further mitigation (per-head clipping and additional calibration samples).
blockers: Need a deterministic reproducer for the worst-case long-context drift to debug per-layer sensitivity (ticketed separately).
Shadow run artifacts require approval for sampling live traffic (privacy/compliance signoff from Security & Privacy).
next_steps: Run 48-hour shadow validation using the top-3 FP8 and top-2 INT8 candidate profiles across both models (redwood-7b, open-13b) on 2025-03-05.
Implement per-layer scale reporting in runtime telemetry to allow automatic fallback for layers that exceed logit-delta thresholds.
Produce a summary matrix (profile x workload) and propose recommended default profiles for runtime-1.20 by 2025-03-18.
Schedule a cross-team review with Product and SRE to decide SLO-tier mappings and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible calibration artifacts for each profile in S3 with README and run parameters recorded.
Shadow validation shows no >1.0 absolute regression in instruction-following pass rate for chosen FP8 profiles.
Latency improvements measurable at p95 for selected profiles and memory savings documented per-host.
Runbook for periodic recalibration (cron + sample size + alert thresholds) committed to Confluence and linked from runtime release notes.
